data.narrative:
Quobly is a seed-stage quantum computing company founded by Maud Vinet, Tristan Meunier, and François Perruchot. The quantum computing sector comprises 3 public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private firms, including mature-stage peers such as Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. The sector contains only 8 private comparables, and filtering by stage (seed), adjacency, or valuation tier yields fewer than 3 datapoints in any narrow cohort. Relying on an all-sector median would conflate seed-stage economics with later-stage, venture-backed firms that have achieved material technical or commercial milestones, introducing substantial bias. No alternative triangulation methods were executable with the available data.

Given the absence of reliable quantitative anchors from comparable analysis, this valuation cannot be supported by the data provided. Any valuation range would require either (1) expansion of the seed-stage peer set through additional market intelligence, (2) application of cost-to-duplicate or discounted cash flow methods using company-specific financials, or (3) explicit stage-to-stage scaling adjustments from later-stage quantum companies—none of which are present here. The primary uncertainty is methodological: the quantum computing sector remains too dispersed and stage-heterogeneous for traditional peer multiples to apply at seed stage.
